picks.why: Nemesius: breathing exists to preserve the innate heat, a doctrine stated plainly.
Roger Bacon on old age: grey hair comes from the weakening of natural heat, the waning the gloss describes.
Petrus de Abano: natural heat is the soul's instrument and resists poisons.
Fludd: calidum innatum by whose power every creature exists, carried in radical moisture.
Zwinger: innate heat and radical moisture as the foundations of all vital functions.

note: idx 6 states the gloss well but opens with OCR garbage; skipped.

picks.why: Paracelsus: the quintessence separated from brandy by water bath, the wine-distillation method.
Reusner: the fifth essence heals sores, fistula and cancer.
Faust: the quintessence draws life and health into the body from the Sun and stars.
Reusner: the art of extracting the fifth essence from quicksilver and vitriol.
Podmore defines odyle/odic force and the sensations of light and temperature it was said to produce.
Reichenbach himself on the polarity of odic light in sunbeams.
Atwood on Od as a 'new imponderable' that few believed in.
Sushruta on the nature of ojas: cool, white, oily, the best seat of life.
Sushruta: ojas permeates the body and its loss brings emaciation and dissolution.
Ojas as the quintessence of all bodily tissues, identified with vital power.
Charaka: in the eighth month ojas passes between mother and foetus.
Vagbhata's rasashastra: a remedy that increases ojas.

note: Natyashastra hits (5, 11) are ojas as literary grandeur, off-sense.

picks.why: Paracelsus himself names sylphs and pygmies against folk names.
Comte de Gabalis: sylphs, gnomes and nymphs are short-lived and seek human company.
Waite: each elemental partakes of one element only and is not a devil.
Guaita: elementals and the dispute over whether they have intelligence.
Conring: the Paracelsians call the four humours empty names, the core doctrinal break.
Libavius berates the Paracelsians for damning Galen and the ancient antidotes.
Colberg: Paracelsists set against Aristotelians and Galenists.
Raphson 1702: the hylozoists and their supposed origin in Strato, as Cudworth framed it.
Blavatsky defines hylozoism as all matter being in some sense alive.
Haeckel traces hylozoism to the Ionian philosophers.
Wundt: philosophical hylozoism taught the eternity of life.
Hathapradipika: uniting prana and apana is pranayama, which is hatha yoga.
Svatmarama: dissolving breath and mind brings liberation.
Hatha yoga as a physiological process preparing the body for higher yoga.
Its lineage through Matsyendranath and Gorakhnath.
Mercuriale defines true gymnastics as a part of medicine.
Felici: the art of gymnastics is necessary to keep the body healthy and strong.
Mercuriale on medical gymnastics as distinct from athletic and military.

note: Most other hits are catalogue entries or citations of Mercuriale's title.

picks.why: Fludd: natural magic seeks heavenly benefits for the body by natural means.
Hildebrand: performing wonders with the aid of natural things.
Roth-Scholtz: hidden virtues of lower things joined to the stars by natural magic.
Oetinger: natural magic as a lost science surviving among Black Forest farmers.

note: Many candidates are title pages or catalogue entries; skipped.

picks.why: The wisdom-fire of candali blazes in the navel, fanned by the winds.
Tummo stirred at the navel melts the bindu, which descends.
Fire arises from the red drop and passes through the central channel.
When the winds stop moving, candali blazes from the navel.
A Korean scholar declines external alchemy (lead and mercury) for preserving his own essence.

note: Most golden-elixir hits are inner alchemy (Zhang Boduan, Chen Zhizun), off-sense for waidan; others are titles or bare mentions.

picks.why: Poliziano: automata were machines that seemed to act of their own accord.
Peucer: art builds automata of iron wheels and weights that imitate the heavens.
Hero's automaton theatres and why they were popular.
Zeising: countless automata invented, back to Daedalus.
